title: CUET PG — Core Subject | Assumptions Conclusions
description: Subject-wise test on Assumptions Conclusions (Core Subject) for CUET PG. 35Q.
subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following is an assumption in the statement: 'If you want to reduce your electricity bill, you should switch off lights and fans when not in use'?

options.text: Switching off lights and fans is the only way to reduce electricity bills.
options.explanation: The statement does not assume exclusivity; it only suggests a method.

options.text: Most people leave lights and fans on when not in use.
options.explanation: The statement does not make any assumptions about people's behavior.

options.text: Electricity is consumed by lights and fans.
options.explanation: This is the core assumption, as the statement links switching off these devices to reducing bills.

options.text: Reducing electricity consumption is the primary goal of individuals.
options.explanation: The statement does not assume anything about individuals' primary goals.

questions.explanation: The statement implies that lights and fans consume electricity, which is why switching them off reduces the bill. This is the underlying assumption.
questions.hint: Consider what the statement assumes about the relationship between lights/fans and electricity consumption.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions logically follows from the statements: 'All intelligent people are creative. Some artists are intelligent.'?

options.text: Only conclusion I follows.
options.explanation: Correct, as explained above.

options.text: Only conclusion II follows.
options.explanation: Conclusion II is incorrect as it makes an unwarranted generalization.

options.text: Both I and II follow.
options.explanation: Only conclusion I follows; conclusion II does not.

options.text: Neither I nor II follows.
options.explanation: Conclusion I does follow, so this option is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Conclusion I ('Some artists are creative') follows because if some artists are intelligent and all intelligent people are creative, then those artists must also be creative. Conclusion II ('All creative people are intelligent') is incorrect as it reverses the given statement without logical basis.
questions.hint: Use Venn diagrams to visualize the relationships between sets.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which assumption is implicit in the notice: 'Please switch off the lights when leaving the room to save electricity.'?

options.text: Employees are capable of understanding the notice.
options.explanation: Correct, as the notice requires comprehension to be effective.

options.text: Employees are concerned about saving electricity.
options.explanation: This is an expectation, not a necessary assumption for the notice to be issued.

options.text: Switching off lights will significantly reduce the electricity bill.
options.explanation: This is a desired outcome, not an assumption for the notice.

options.text: The office management wants to reduce costs.
options.explanation: This is the motive behind the notice, not an assumption for its effectiveness.

questions.explanation: The notice assumes that employees can understand the instruction. Without this assumption, the notice would be ineffective. Other options are either expectations or outcomes, not fundamental assumptions for the notice to function.
questions.hint: Consider what must be true for the notice to be meaningful.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions logically follows from the statement: 'The prices of essential commodities are rising at an alarming rate.'?

options.text: Only conclusion I follows.
options.explanation: Conclusion I is an overgeneralization and does not necessarily follow.

options.text: Only conclusion II follows.
options.explanation: Conclusion II is an opinion, not a logical conclusion.

options.text: Both I and II follow.
options.explanation: Neither conclusion follows directly from the statement.

options.text: Neither I nor II follows.
options.explanation: Correct, as neither conclusion is a direct logical consequence of the statement.

questions.explanation: Conclusion I ('People will find it difficult to survive') is an overgeneralization and cannot be definitively concluded from the statement. Conclusion II ('The government should intervene to control prices') is an opinion, not a logical conclusion. Neither conclusion follows directly from the given statement.
questions.hint: Evaluate whether the conclusions are directly supported by the statement or are assumptions/opinions.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following is an implicit assumption in the advertisement: 'Our new 'SmartClean' detergent removes 99% of germs and leaves your clothes sparkling clean.'?

options.text: Consumers are concerned about germ removal in their laundry.
options.explanation: Correct, as the ad emphasizes this feature to appeal to consumers.

options.text: Other detergents do not remove 99% of germs.
options.explanation: This is a competitive claim, not an implicit assumption for the ad's effectiveness.

options.text: Sparkling clean clothes are a primary concern for all consumers.
options.explanation: This is an overgeneralization; the ad does not assume this for all consumers.

options.text: The detergent is affordable for all segments of society.
options.explanation: This is about market strategy, not an implicit assumption in the ad.

questions.explanation: The advertisement assumes that consumers value germ removal in their laundry, as it highlights this feature to appeal to potential buyers. Other options are either competitive claims or overgeneralizations.
questions.hint: Identify what the advertiser must believe about consumer preferences for the ad to be effective.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions logically follows from the statement: 'Exposure to loud noise can cause hearing impairment.'?

options.text: Only conclusion I follows.
options.explanation: Correct, as conclusion I is a logical and practical inference.

options.text: Only conclusion II follows.
options.explanation: Conclusion II is an overgeneralization and incorrect.

options.text: Both I and II follow.
options.explanation: Only conclusion I follows; conclusion II does not.

options.text: Neither I nor II follows.
options.explanation: Conclusion I does follow, so this option is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Conclusion I ('People working in noisy environments should use ear protection') is a logical inference to prevent potential harm. Conclusion II ('All hearing impairments are caused by loud noise') is incorrect as it generalizes the statement beyond its scope.
questions.hint: Determine which conclusion is a practical and direct inference from the statement.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following is an assumption underlying the municipal corporation's decision to privatize waste collection services?

options.text: Private companies are inherently more efficient than government bodies in waste collection.
options.explanation: This is a general belief, not the underlying assumption for the decision.

options.text: The current waste collection service provided by the municipal corporation is inefficient.
options.explanation: Correct, as the decision is made to improve efficiency, implying the current service is inadequate.

options.text: Privatization will lead to a reduction in the cost of waste collection for citizens.
options.explanation: This is a desired outcome, not the assumption underlying the decision.

options.text: The quality of waste collection service will definitely improve after privatization.
options.explanation: This is a hoped-for outcome, not the assumption for the decision.

questions.explanation: The decision assumes that the current waste collection service is inefficient, as the goal is to 'improve efficiency.' Other options are either general beliefs or desired outcomes, not the underlying assumption for the decision.
questions.hint: Identify what must be true for the decision to make sense.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions can be drawn from the statement: 'A recent study showed that students who regularly consume energy drinks tend to perform better in exams than those who do not.'?

options.text: Energy drinks enhance academic performance.
options.explanation: The study shows correlation, not causation.

options.text: Students who perform better in exams are more likely to consume energy drinks.
options.explanation: This is reverse causation, which the study does not establish.

options.text: There is a correlation between energy drink consumption and exam performance.
options.explanation: Correct, as the study directly establishes this relationship.

options.text: To improve exam performance, students should consume energy drinks.
options.explanation: The study does not imply a recommendation or causation.

questions.explanation: The statement establishes a correlation between energy drink consumption and exam performance. It does not imply causation (option A), reverse causation (option B), or a definitive recommendation (option D).
questions.hint: Identify what the study directly establishes between the two variables.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the corporation's decision to impose a heavy toll on private vehicles entering the city center during peak hours to reduce traffic congestion?

options.text: Public transport will be sufficient to handle the increased demand.
options.explanation: This is not an assumption but a potential outcome. The statement does not imply this as a given.

options.text: People will prefer to use public transport or avoid peak hour travel due to the toll.
options.explanation: This is the core assumption behind the decision, as the toll is expected to influence behavior and reduce congestion.

options.text: The revenue generated from the toll will be used for road maintenance.
options.explanation: This is unrelated to the assumption about reducing traffic congestion.

options.text: Traffic congestion is primarily caused by private vehicles.
options.explanation: While this may be true, it is not an assumption implicit in the decision to impose the toll.

questions.explanation: The assumption here is that people will change their behavior due to the toll, either by using public transport or avoiding peak hour travel, which is expected to reduce congestion.
questions.hint: Consider what the municipal corporation expects to happen as a result of the toll.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Which of the following is an assumption underlying the statement: 'All politicians are corrupt because they accept money from lobbyists.'

options.text: Lobbyists only give money to corrupt politicians.
options.explanation: This is not an assumption; it is a conclusion that may or may not be true.

options.text: Accepting money from lobbyists is a sign of corruption.
options.explanation: This directly states the assumption that accepting money correlates with corruption.

options.text: All people who accept money are corrupt.
options.explanation: This is too absolute and not necessarily implied by the statement.

options.text: No politician refuses money from lobbyists.
options.explanation: This is irrelevant to the assumption about corruption.

questions.explanation: The assumption is that accepting money from lobbyists directly correlates with corruption. Option B states this clearly. Options A and C are too absolute, and D is irrelevant to the given statement.
questions.hint: Focus on the direct relationship between accepting money and corruption.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Statement: 'The school has decided to introduce mandatory yoga classes because it improves students' mental health.' Which of the following is NOT an assumption in the above statement?

options.text: Yoga can improve mental health.
options.explanation: This is a necessary assumption for the statement to make sense.

options.text: Students' mental health needs improvement.
options.explanation: This is a necessary assumption for the school's action to be justified.

options.text: Yoga is the only way to improve mental health.
options.explanation: This is not an assumption; the statement does not claim exclusivity.

options.text: The school has the resources to implement yoga classes.
options.explanation: This is a practical assumption for the school's decision.

questions.explanation: The statement does not imply that yoga is the only way to improve mental health. It is a possible method, but not the only one. The other options are directly related to the assumption behind the statement.
questions.hint: Identify the assumption that is not logically necessary for the statement to hold.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Statement: 'The company’s profits increased this quarter because of the new marketing strategy.' Assumption: The new marketing strategy was the primary cause of the profit increase. Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the assumption?

options.text: The company launched a new product line this quarter.
options.explanation: This could also contribute to profits but does not directly weaken the marketing strategy assumption.

options.text: The economy experienced a boom this quarter, leading to higher sales across the industry.
options.explanation: This provides an alternative cause for the profit increase, weakening the marketing strategy assumption.

options.text: Competitors also saw an increase in profits this quarter.
options.explanation: This does not directly weaken the assumption about the marketing strategy.

options.text: The marketing strategy was expensive to implement.
options.explanation: This does not address the cause of the profit increase.

questions.explanation: Option B suggests an alternative reason (economic boom) for the profit increase, thereby weakening the assumption that the marketing strategy was the primary cause.
questions.hint: Look for an alternative cause that could explain the profit increase.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Statement: 'To reduce traffic congestion, the city should implement congestion pricing.' What is the assumption in the above statement?

options.text: People will change their travel behavior if they have to pay for driving in congested areas.
options.explanation: This is the core assumption behind congestion pricing.

options.explanation: This is an extreme claim not implied by the statement.

options.explanation: This is an exaggerated and unsupported claim.

options.text: The city has enough public transportation to accommodate displaced drivers.
options.explanation: This is not a necessary assumption for the statement.

questions.explanation: The assumption is that pricing will influence behavior (Option A). The other options make extreme claims that are not implied by the statement.
questions.hint: Consider what must be true for congestion pricing to reduce traffic.
questions.subject: cuet-pg-core

questions.question: Statement: 'The new drug is effective because it reduces symptoms in 90% of patients within 48 hours.' Which of the following is a valid assumption?

options.text: The drug has no side effects.

options.text: The reduction in symptoms is due to the drug and not other factors.

options.explanation: The statement only mentions symptom reduction, not complete recovery.

options.explanation: This is irrelevant to the statement about effectiveness.

questions.question: Statement: 'The athlete won the race because she trained harder than her competitors.' What is the assumption in the above statement?

options.text: The athlete had the best natural ability.
options.explanation: This is not mentioned or assumed in the statement.

options.text: The race was not affected by external factors like weather.
options.explanation: This is irrelevant to the assumption about training.

options.explanation: This is the core assumption linking training to winning.

options.explanation: This is an extreme and unsupported claim.

questions.question: Statement: 'The restaurant’s revenue increased after it changed its menu.' Assumption: The menu change was responsible for the increase in revenue. Which of the following, if true, would strengthen the assumption?

questions.question: Statement: 'The team lost the match because the captain was injured.' Which of the following is a valid conclusion from the statement?

questions.question: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument that 'private coaching classes are the primary factor in achieving high scores in the national entrance exam'?

options.text: The national entrance exam is known for its high difficulty level.
options.explanation: This does not address the causal link between coaching and high scores.

options.text: Many students who attend private coaching classes also spend more time studying independently.
options.explanation: This introduces another factor but does not necessarily weaken the primary role of coaching.

options.text: The fees for private coaching classes are prohibitively expensive for most students.
options.explanation: This is irrelevant to the causal link between coaching and high scores.

options.text: Students who enroll in private coaching classes generally have a stronger academic background and higher motivation.
options.explanation: This provides an alternative explanation for high scores, weakening the argument that coaching is the primary factor.

questions.explanation: The argument assumes that coaching is the primary factor in high scores. Introducing an alternative explanation, such as students with stronger academic backgrounds being more likely to attend coaching, weakens this assumption.
questions.hint: Look for a confounding variable that provides an alternative explanation for the observed correlation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements must be false based on the premises: 'No cars are airplanes. All airplanes are vehicles. Some vehicles are motorcycles.'?

options.text: Some vehicles are cars.
options.explanation: This could be true, as cars are a subset of vehicles.

options.text: Some motorcycles are not airplanes.
options.explanation: This could be true, as motorcycles are a subset of vehicles, and vehicles are not airplanes.

options.text: All motorcycles are cars.
options.explanation: This must be false, as it would imply an overlap between cars and airplanes, which contradicts the premise that no cars are airplanes.

options.text: No cars are vehicles.
options.explanation: This contradicts the premise that all airplanes are vehicles and no cars are airplanes, implying cars are not vehicles.

questions.explanation: From the premises, we know that cars and airplanes are mutually exclusive (no overlap), and motorcycles are a subset of vehicles. Therefore, it is impossible for all motorcycles to be cars, as this would imply an overlap between cars and airplanes, which contradicts the first premise.
questions.hint: Use Venn diagrams to visualize the relationships between the sets and identify the contradiction.
